description: Parte de Club Ohana del Matías Ramón Mella
details:
Since the beginning of space exploration, humanity has sent numerous technologies into space to investigate, discover, and expand our understanding of the universe. Throughout these missions, equipment has been left behind on the Moon, Mars, and other locations in the solar system. Some devices completed their missions and reached the end of their operational life, while others continue to function or travel through space. These artifacts are part of the legacy of human exploration, yet their stories remain largely unknown to younger generations.

**OHANA SPACE** seeks to bring these stories closer to children and young people through an educational, creative, and accessible experience. Our project transforms scientific information and data provided by NASA into engaging narratives that explain the purpose of space equipment, the missions it supported, and its contribution to scientific discovery.

Our main educational resource is the children's story **“Letters from the Dust” (Cartas desde el polvo)**, developed in three versions: digital, printed, and Braille. Through Lu, a curious girl who discovers the secrets of space alongside her grandfather, readers learn about the machines and artifacts that remained on the Moon and Mars after space missions. The Braille edition reinforces our commitment to inclusion by allowing children with visual impairments to access and enjoy the same story.

The story and its digital resources were developed using **Canva and Book Creator**, with support from **Claude and ChatGPT** during the creative and content-development process. We also created animations using **Canva AI**, incorporating NASA-provided scientific data to enrich the presentation of the missions and their technological artifacts.

The project combines storytelling, digital publishing, visual animation, and science communication to make complex scientific information easier for children to understand. Its creative approach lies in turning the legacy of space technology into a narrative experience that connects scientific facts with imagination, curiosity, and inclusive learning.

OHANA SPACE aims to strengthen scientific literacy, encourage interest in space exploration and STEM fields, and promote equal opportunities to access scientific knowledge. By offering different reading formats and combining educational storytelling with digital resources, we seek to make space exploration more engaging and accessible to diverse audiences.
